acceptance: Red test first: with the four failure blocks of cycle 2035 and the fixability stage at enforce, the cycle stops after audit round 1 with the outcome handed-off and runs no repair round.
At shadow each component records its signal (REPAIR_HANDOFF, CYCLE_SPEND_LIMIT, CYCLE_SUPERSEDED, LADDER_AUDIT_FIX with audit_fix_handler registered) and the flow of today runs.
A cycle sealed handed-off or superseded writes the salvage pointer of its worktree, and the failure drain does not charge the item as a lane capability failure.
evolve wave status shows each handed-off and superseded cycle with its reason.
fix: Call fixability before each repair round (computeRetryEnvelope callers) and seal a stop as handed-off with the salvage pointer. Ask cyclespend and supersede at each phase boundary and seal superseded or handed-off. Register the audit_fix handler with core.WithRungHandler(retryladder.RungAuditFix, h) at the composition root. Each call obeys its own stage key.
notes: Route console-manual: build_explanation_handoff.go, orchestrator.go, cyclerun.go and phases/audit/audit.go are on the fence (integrity_surface.go:87, :99, :100, :140). Wire each lane package as soon as it lands; the deps list all four only for the last step.
source: console, 2026-10-27, operator request on cycle 2035 ("balance to cost and output"). ADR-0158; plan docs/plans/cost-aware-repair-2026-10.md
summary: The lane items repair-fixability-handoff, cycle-spend-limit-stop-and-handoff, cycle-stops-when-console-takes-its-item and audit-fix-rung-handler build pure packages. Their call sites are on the fence: the retry envelope callers and the phase loop in internal/core, the cycle seal, the composition root of the orchestrator and the audit session.
title: Wire the fixability stop, the spend limit, the supersede check and the audit_fix handler into the cycle (ADR-0158)
